transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-21 10:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (CTO, SorinTech), Jenna Ortiz (SRE), Luis Ramirez (ML Eng)
Links shared: deck https://redwood.app/decks/sorintech-poc | latency spreadsheet link (to be shared) | runbook: https://redwood.app/runbooks/dedicated-slot

Auto-summary (auto): Redwood median lat 22-28% lower on 1k token tests; throughput gains when batching enabled; incumbent wins occasionally at very small-batch low qps due to cheaper per-token in that config.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick check, can you hear us?
[00:06] Mark (CTO): yes loud and clear, thanks. we pulled the team in — jenna and luis are here.
[00:12] Priya (SE): awesome. today's agenda — go over last week's bench runs, look at the head-to-head against the incumbent, touch on routing/fallback, then agree next steps for a dedicated load run.
[00:25] Jenna (SRE): sounds good. for context we ran two slices overnight: steady 50 qps, and burst 250 qps for 15 minutes. included 3 model sizes and our usual prompt set.
[00:36] Alex (AE): perfect. ok priya, you want to pull up the numbers?
[00:40] Priya (SE): yeah i'll share my screen — i'm gonna call out the median p50/p95 numbers first — note, transcription may flip a few names, sorry if i mumble. on the 1k token baseline workload Redwood p50 was 120ms vs incumbent 155ms so about 22% improvement; p95 420ms vs 580ms — roughly 28%
[01:05] Luis (ML Eng): those are pretty consistent with what we saw in the lab last week, though our prod-like traces have a heavier long-tail, so p99 matters a lot. what did p99 look like?
[01:16] Priya (SE): p99 was 1.2s on Redwood vs 1.7s incumbent for this test. caveat: these were with batch sizes set to 8 for aggregate runs. when we did single-request flow (no batching) the incumbent's cold-path was slightly faster — like 10-15% — because of their tiny-optimized kernels.
[01:34] Mark (CTO): interesting, so batching is where we get the 1.8x throughput number you mentioned?
[01:38] Priya (SE): yeah exactly. in our burst 15-min tests, Redwood sustained 1.8x higher overall tokens/sec when batching was enabled and KV cache warm. note we saw an ingestion hiccup at minute 7 in one run — i'm still binned on that — the log shows a routing fallback that triggered to a smaller instance class.
[01:55] Jenna (SRE): that fallback is a worry — can we control the routing thresholds? we don't want silent fallbacks in prod.
[02:00] Alex (AE): totally. there's a routing playbook and we can make thresholds explicit — we'll add a canary-only flag and email alerts on fallback. priya can you outline the rollback/fallback policies?
[02:10] Priya (SE): sure — we support policy tiers: strict (no fallback offsite), relaxed (allow variant with quantize), and opportunistic (cost-saving fallbacks). for this POC we used relaxed — that explains the one fallback. we recommend strict for stage; for prod you choose.
[02:26] Luis (ML Eng): question on quantization — the incumbent mentioned 4-bit for some models; you showed a FP16-compromise earlier. what's the quality delta?
[02:34] Priya (SE): in our evals for your prompt set, 4-bit caused a few hallucination patterns on longer context; FP16/8-bit mixed gave the best cost/quality. we'll share the quant table. note: transcription might say quanta or quan-tize as quanta — apologies.
[02:50] Mark (CTO): ops/security — SOC2 and KMS. we need evidence for audit and must ensure keys remain customer managed.
[02:58] Alex (AE): Redwood Private supports customer KMS and HSM; we can provide SOC2 report and a redacted audit trail. i'll send the security bundle after the call.
[03:06] Jenna (SRE): also need VPC peering details — network egress patterns, ports.
[03:11] Priya (SE): i'll drop the VPC diagrams in the runbook. we've seen folks misread KV cache as KV cash in notes before — but yes, it's KV cache and it's within the VPC when you run private.
[03:23] Mark (CTO): back to perf — show us the unit cost comparison when we enable batching vs when we don't. so we can make a tradeoff decision.
[03:31] Priya (SE): good call — we calculated unit-cost/token for the three slices. with batching: Redwood $0.00037/token vs incumbent $0.00049/token. no-batching small-qps: Redwood $0.00062 vs incumbent $0.00058 (incumbent slightly cheaper there). i'll attach the CSV.
[03:52] Luis (ML Eng): ok that's useful. can we see per-route breakdown? some routes are short prompts, others are 800-1k tokens.
[03:59] Alex (AE): we'll send per-route; that's one of the next steps.
[04:04] Jenna (SRE): outage scenarios: if region goes down, do you support automatic regional failover? and what's RTO?
[04:11] Priya (SE): yes, smart routing with policy-based fallbacks. RTO depends on your policy — for strict SLOs we keep warm slots in cold-standby region so failover under 30s; for lower tiers it's minutes.
[04:22] Mark (CTO): what about data residency — can we pin everything to eu-west-1?
[04:28] Alex (AE): yes on Dedicated/Private we can pin regions. hosted has region options too. we'll include region pinning notes in the follow-up.
[04:36] Priya (SE): quick note on the one regression we saw: during the 250 qps burst some requests hit a quantization path that spiked p95 in run #3 — that was due to an auto-kernel fallback that misselected a slower kernel on one GPU type. we've opened an internal ticket to force the right kernel selector for that model.
[04:56] Mark (CTO): that's important, we rely on consistent tail latency. is there a way to lock kernel selection per-deploy?
[05:02] Priya (SE): yes we can pin kernel profiles per model version in the deployment config. we'll share the exact config snippet.
[05:10] Luis (ML Eng): can Redwood replicate our exact traffic pattern for the load test? we have a 60/40 split of short to long prompts during business hours.
[05:17] Alex (AE): yes please upload the 24-hour trace — Priya will set up a dedicated slot and run the 1-hour focused load to emulate that distribution.
[05:25] Priya (SE): scheduling question — is next Tue at 13:00 UTC acceptable?
[05:29] Mark (CTO): works for us, we'll confirm after i check with ops.
[05:33] Jenna (SRE): on observability — we want per-token tracing and SLIs exported to our datadog. can we push traces?
[05:40] Priya (SE): yes we support pushing traces via OTLP endpoint and exporting token-level cost metrics. we'll add the datadog config to the runbook.
[05:48] Alex (AE): ok let's recap next steps quickly — i'll list them.
[05:52] Alex (AE): 1) Redwood sends latency/cost per-route CSV and runbook links by 2027-09-23. 2) Priya schedules and provisions dedicated slot for 1-hour load test, shares runbook and slack invite. 3) SorinTech (Luis) uploads 24h traffic trace and top-10 prompt set by 2027-09-24. 4) Redwood sends SOC2 & KMS evidence package redacted copy.
[06:18] Mark (CTO): perfect. any blockers on Redwood side?
[06:22] Priya (SE): we have capacity for the load run, just need the trace and final confirm on the time.
[06:27] Alex (AE): i'll follow up with an email and the pricing/latency sheet. thanks everyone.
[06:31] Jenna (SRE): thanks all.
[06:33] Luis (ML Eng): thanks. bye.

Notes: occasional transcription glitches present (names and acronyms sometimes auto-corrected). Action items captured above.
